364.text: Na ⁺ / K ⁺ pump is associated with
364.sol: Sodium-potassium pump ( Na ⁺- K ⁺ ) is a membrane transport protein that exchanges sodium ions ( Na ⁺ ) for potassium ions ( K ⁺ ) . It transports 3 Na ⁺ outwards for 2 ~K ⁺ into the cell, thus maintaining the differential concentrations of each ion across the plasma membrane. The process requires energy in the form of ATP, being a form of active transport.

73934.subject: General Ability
73934.text: Which of the following statements regarding animal cell membrane is correct?
options: They are composed of phospholipids only.
They are composed of proteins only.
They are composed of phospholipids and proteins only.
They are composed of phospholipids, proteins and cholesterol (lipid).
73934.sol: The cell membrane of animal cells is primarily composed of phospholipids, which form a bilayer structure. Embedded within or attached to this phospholipid bilayer are proteins that serve various functions like transport and signaling. Additionally, cholesterol molecules are interspersed among the phospholipids, contributing to the membrane's stability and fluidity. This composition of phospholipids, proteins, and cholesterol allows the cell membrane to regulate the passage of molecules and ions, maintain cell shape

73936.subject: General Ability
73936.text: Which of the following is not a part of compounds microscope?
73936.sol: A compound microscope typically consists of several parts including a mirror or light source (to illuminate the specimen), a stage (where the specimen is placed), clips (to hold the specimen slide in place), objective lenses (to magnify the specimen), an eyepiece or ocular lens (through which the observer views the specimen), and focusing knobs (to bring the specimen into sharp focus). The retina, however, is a part of the eye and not a component of the compound microscope.

74000.subject: General Ability
74000.text: A liquid is heated up to a certain temperature. Which one of the following situation would correspond to the boiling of the liquid ?
options: When atmospheric pressure becomes equal to the vapour pressure
When atmospheric pressure becomes Jess than vapour pressure
When atmospheric pressure becomes higher than the vapour pressure
When vapour pressure becomes equal to the air pressure
74000.sol: When atmospheric pressure becomes equal to the vapour pressure.

74251.subject: General Ability
74251.text: Which one of the following statements regarding Ohm's law is not correct?
options: Ohm's law is an assumption that current through a conductor is always directly proportional to the potential d
A conducting device obeys Ohm's law when the resistance of a device is independent of magnitude and polarity o
A conducting material obeys Ohm's law when the resistance of material is independent of the magnitude and dire
All homogeneous materials obey Ohm's law irrespective of whether the field is within range or strong
74251.sol: All homogeneous materials like conductors, semiconductors obey Ohm's law within limited range of electric field. In the case of strong field, there are departures from Ohm's law.

74281.subject: General Ability
74281.text: In an incandescent electric bulb, the filament of the bulb is made up of which metal?
74281.sol: The filament is the part of the light bulb that produces light. Filaments in incandescent light bulbs are made of tungsten. Whenever an electric current goes through the filament, the filament glows. The reason tungsten is used is because it has the highest melting temperature of any element at 3600 K . For a typical incandescent light bulb, the Tungsten filament operates at approximately 2500 Celsius. Hence, the filaments are made of tungsten.

74323.subject: General Ability
74323.text: On exposure to moist air, copper gains a green coat on its surface due to formation of which one of the following compounds ?
74323.sol: Copper metal when exposed to air turns green in colour due to corrosion. When copper vessel is exposed to air in rainy season, the metal reacts with gases and moisture and atmospheric gases to form a mixture of copper carbonate and copper hydroxide. This gives a green colour to the surface of copper metal. The reaction is as follows: 2 Cu + H ₂ O + CO ₂+ O ₂ Cu ( OH )₂+ CuCO ₃

74427.subject: General Ability
74427.text: Which one of the following elements corrodes rapidly?
74427.sol: Iron corrodes rapidly, because of its non-stable corrosion products on the surface. Rust occurs when metals containing iron react with the oxygen in the air or in water and form a compound called iron(III) oxide (ferric oxide). This compound contains water molecules, so we call it a hydrated compound. Both oxygen gas and water must be present for the iron to rust. Chemically and very simply speaking, iron atoms lose a few electrons to oxygen atoms. This process by which electrons are removed from atoms is called ox

74430.subject: General Ability
74430.text: Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the code given below the Lists: array llll & array l Lists I (Disease) array & & array l Lists II (Remedy) array A. & Hypermetropia & 1. & Concave lens B. & Presbyopia & 2. & Bifocal lens C. & Myopia & 3. & Surgery D. & Cataract & 4. & Convex lens array
74430.sol: Hypermetropia, sometimes called hyperopia, is the term used to define being longsighted. Myopia is the term used to define being shortsighted. A myopic person has clear vision when looking at objects close to them, but distant objects will appear blurred. Presbyopia is when your eyes gradually lose the ability to see things clearly up close. It is a normal part of aging. Contaract is a condition in which the clarity of the natural lens reduces. Lens of the eye becomes Opaque.

74465.sol: As the light enters from rarer medium to the denser medium the speed of light decreases but the frequency remains the same.

74513.sol: Soaps are sodium or potassium salts of some long chain carboxylic acids, e.g. Stearic acid, Oleic acid and Palmitic acid.

74663.subject: General Ability
74663.text: When you walk on a woolen carpet and bring your finger near the metallic handle of a door an electric shock is produced. This is because
options: charge is transferred from your body to the handle
a chemical reaction occurs when you touch the handle
the temperature of the human body is higher than that of the handle
the human body and the handle arrive at thermal equilibrium by the process
74663.sol: All materials are made up of negatively- and positivelycharged particles. These usually exist in equal amounts, balancing each other out. But when two materials come into contact, one may 'steal' negatively-charged electrons from the other. One material ends up with more negative charges than positive ones, meaning that it becomes negatively-charged overall, whilst the other becomes positively-charged. If the charges cannot move away as they are produced, they accumulate in the material as static charge, or electri

75331.sol: Quinary activities are the activities or services that focus on the creation, re-arrangement and interpretation of new and existing ideas. It also include data interpretation and the use and evaluation of new technologies.

75538.subject: General Ability
75538.text: The Munda language group belongs to which family?
75538.sol: Munda languages belong to the Austroasiatic family. Some authors consider them as a subfamily coordinate with Mon-Khmer.

75864.subject: General Ability
75864.text: The word 'Secular' was inserted into the Constitution of India by:
75864.sol: Secularism in India means equal treatment of all religions by the state. With the 42nd Amendment of the Constitution of India enacted in 1976, the Preamble to the Constitution asserted that India is a secular nation. However, neither India's constitution nor its laws define the relationship between religion and state.

79354.subject: Botany
79354.text: Match List I with List II : List I List II A. Conjunctive tissue I. Specialised cells in the vicinity of guard cells B. Casparian strips II. Endodermal cells rich in starch C. Subsidiary cells III. Tissue between xylem and phloem D. Starch sheath IV. Endodermal cells with suberin deposition Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
79354.sol: Conjunctive tissue is the parenchymatous tissue present between the xylem and phloem in roots. Casparian strips are the water-impermeable, waxy suberin depositions present on the radial and tangential walls of endodermal cells. Subsidiary cells are the specialised epidermal cells present in the vicinity of guard cells. Starch sheath is the endodermis of a dicot stem, as its cells are rich in starch grains. Thus, the correct match is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II. Answer: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

79369.subject: Botany
79369.text: Plants having little or no secondary growth are
79369.sol: The tissues responsible for the increase in girth of plants comprises secondary growth. Such tissues include two types of lateral meristem: vascular cambium and cork cambium. Secondary growth is primarily observed in dicots. Monocots do not undergo secondary growth. In the given options, grasses are monocot and have closed type of vascular bundle, therefore, they do not show secondary growth.

79569.subject: Botany
79569.text: Which among the following is not a prokaryote?
79569.sol: Among the given options, Saccharomyces is the scientific name of yeast belongs to kingdom Fungi, i.e. it is a eukaryote. They possess a well-defined nucleus and other cell organelles. Nostoc and Oscillatoria are cyanobacteria, while Mycobacterium is a true bacterium. Cyanobacteria and bacteria both are prokaryotes as they lack a well-defined nucleus and other cell organelles. They belong to the kingdom Monera.

80270.subject: Botany
80270.sol: Vernalization is a process of shortening of juvenile or vegetative phase and hastening flowering by a previous cold treatment. Example-henbane, carrot, cabbage.

80407.subject: Botany

In ETC (Electron Transport Chain), one molecule of NADH + H + gives rise to 2 ATP molecules, and one FADH 2 gi

Oxidation-reduction reactions produce proton gradients in respiration.

82195.subject: Physics
82195.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Atoms are electrically neutral as they contain equal number of positive and negative charges. Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
82195.sol: Statement I is true as atoms are electrically neutral because they contain equal number of positive and negative charges. Statement II is wrong as atom of most of the elements are stable and emit characteristic spectrum. But this statement is not true for every atom.

83908.subject: Zoology
83908.text: Genetic engineering has been successfully used for producing
options: transgenic mice for testing safety of polio vaccine before use in humans
transgenic models for studying new treatments for certain cardiac diseases
transgenic cow-Rosie which produces high fat milk for making ghee
animals like bulls for farm work as they have super power
83908.sol: Transgenic mice are being developed for use in testing the safety of vaccines before they are used on humans. Transgenic mice are being used for testing toxicity of drugs. Transgenic animals are made that carry genes, which make them more sensitive to toxic substances than non-transgenic animals. They are then exposed to the toxic substances and the effects studied. Toxicity testing in such animals will allow us to obtain results in less time.

84216.subject: Zoology
84216.text: Which of the following statements related to pituitary gland are correct ? (a) It is divided anatomically into adenohypophysis and neurohypophysis (b) It secretes follicle stimulating hormone (c) It secretes melanocyte stimulating hormone (d) It does not secrete prolactin Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
84216.sol: The pituitary gland is anatomically divided into the adenohypophysis and the neurohypophysis. Thus, statement (a) is correct. The adenohypophysis consists of the pars distalis and the pars intermedia. The pars distalis (anterior pituitary) secretes several hormones, including Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH) and Prolactin (PRL). Thus, statement (b) is correct and statement (d) is incorrect. The pars intermedia secretes Melanocyte Stimulating Hormone (MSH). Thus, statement (c) is correct. Therefore, statements (a)

84274.subject: Zoology
84274.sol: Melanin protects skin from the sun's ultraviolet rays. These can burn the skin and reduce its elasticity, leading to premature aging. People tan because sunlight causes the skin to produce more melanin and darken. Related Theory:- The basal cell layer contains cells called melanocytes. Melanocytes produce the skin pigment known as melanin, which gives skin its tan or brown colour.

84497.subject: Zoology
84497.text: Infection of Ascaris usually occurs by
options: drinking water containing egg of Ascaris
84497.sol: Infection of Ascaris occurs in a healthy person due to contaminated water, vegetables, fruits, etc. Mosquitos bite causes malaria due to the entry to Plasmodium parasite into the blood. Eating imperfectly cooked pork causes trichinosis disease (parasitic disease). Tse-tse fly causes trypanosomiasis, on infection of the central nervous system.

84524.subject: Zoology
84524.text: Which one of the following is a hallucinogenic drug?
84524.sol: LSD is a psychedelic drug causing optical and auditory hallucination and induces behavioural abnormalities. Opium and morphine are opiate narcotics and acts as depressants and analgesic. Caffeine is a stimulant. Related Theory Drug addiction can be due to - Stress, Curiosity, Peer pressure, To overcome frustrations and depressions, etc.

84757.sol: Azotobacter, Oscillatoria, Anabaena and Nostoc can fix nitrogen but Volvox cannot fix nitrogen.

85296.subject: Zoology
85296.text: In which mode of inheritance do you expect more maternal influence among the offspring?
85296.sol: During fertilisation, mother contribute its nucleus as well as the cytoplasm. However, father sperm consist only nucleus. Thus, the cytoplasmic inheritance is also called maternal inheritance. Genes located on Y-chromosome show Y-linked inheritance. This carries the paternal influences. A gene located in the X-chromosome shows X -linked inheritance. 115738.subject: Chemistry
115738.text: In what way does ozone help to improve the quality of certain products mentioned in the passage?
115738.sol: Ozone is used in applications such as sterilizing water and disinfection, which can help reduce the risk of spoilage and improve the quality and safety of various products.

116035.subject: Chemistry
116035.text: How does livermorium occur in nature?
options: As a decay product of thorium and uranium minerals
116035.sol: The paragraph explains that livermorium is a synthetic radioactive element, indicating that it does not occur naturally.

116169.subject: Chemistry
116169.text: Why does F 2 have a smaller enthalpy of dissociation compared to Cl 2 ?
116169.sol: F 2 has a smaller enthalpy of dissociation compared to Cl 2 due to the relatively large electron-electron repulsion among the lone pairs in the F 2 molecule, where they are much closer to each other than in the case of Cl 2 .**

116171.subject: Chemistry
116171.text: What is the important property of white phosphorus known as "chemiluminescence"?
options: Its ability to dissolve in water
Its ability to glow in the dark
116171.sol: The paragraph mentions that white phosphorus exhibits "chemiluminescence," which means it has the ability to glow in the dark.

116191.subject: Chemistry
116191.text: Statement (A) Among the oxides of nitrogen, NO and NO ₂ are paramagnetic. Statement (B) NO is paramagnetic in the gaseous state and diamagnetic in liquid state. The correct answer is
options: (A) is correct, ( B ) is not correct
Both ( A ) and ( B ) are not correct
116191.sol: Statement (A) Among the oxides of nitrogen, NO and NO ₂ are paramagnetic is the correct statement as N -atom contains unpaired electrons in its structure. Statement (B) NO is paramagnetic in gaseous state and diamagnetic in liquid-state is also the correct statement as NO in liquid state exists as dimer with no unpaired electron in the structure. Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

116576.subject: Chemistry
116576.text: How does hydrochloric acid affect actinoid metals?
options: It has no effect on them

116760.subject: Chemistry
116760.text: What accounts for the formation of Eu2+?
options: The loss of two s electrons
The presence of a completely filled f subshell
The strong reducing properties of europium
The high ionization enthalpy of europium
116760.sol: Eu2+ is formed by losing the two s electrons.

116836.subject: Chemistry
116836.text: What are some individual lanthanoid oxides used for in applications involving light emission?
116836.sol: Some individual Ln oxides are used as phosphors in television screens and similar fluorescing surfaces.

116837.subject: Chemistry
116837.text: What is the role of manganese(II) ions in speeding up the oxidation of water by potassium permanganate?
options: They act as a reducing agent.
They have no effect on the reaction.
116837.sol: Manganese(II) ions or the presence of zinc sulfate or zinc oxide can catalyze the oxidation of water by potassium permanganate.

116879.subject: Chemistry
116879.text: Assertion: Transition metals and their complexes show catalytic activity. Reason: The activation energy of a reaction is lowered by the catalyst.
options: Assertion is true. Reason is true and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion
Assertion is true. Reason is true but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion
Assertion is true but Reason is false
Assertion is false but Reason is true
116879.sol: The transition metals and their compounds are known for their catalytic activity. This activity is ascribed to their ability to adopt multiple oxidation states and to form complexes. Catalysts at a solid surface involve the formation of bonds between reactant molecules and atoms of the surface of the catalyst (first row transition metals utilise 3d and 4s electrons for bonding). This has the effect of increasing the concentration of the reactants at the catalyst surface and also weakening of the bonds in the reacti

117147.subject: Chemistry
117147.text: Copper sulphate is dissolved in water containing for making Bordeaux mixture.
117147.sol: Bordeaux mixture consists of copper sulphate ( CuSO ₄ ) and lime [ Ca ( OH )₂ ] .

117531.subject: Chemistry
117531.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as “Assertion A” and the other is labelled as “Reason R” Assertion A : In the complex Ni ( CO ) 4 and Fe ( CO ) 5 , the metals have zero oxidation state. Reason R : Low oxidation states are found when a complex has ligands capable of π -donor character in addition to the σ -bonding. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the option
options: A is correct but R is not correct
A is not correct but R is correct
Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
117531.sol: The ligand carbon monoxide has no charge, hence metals have zero oxidation state in both Ni ( CO ) 4 and Fe ( CO ) 5 . Low oxidation states are found when a complex has ligands capable of π -acceptor character in addition to the σ -bonding. In the complexes, Ni CO 4 & Fe CO 5 , the ligand CO is π - acceptor character in addition to the σ - bonding .

117872.subject: Chemistry
117872.text: How many ions obtain after dissociation of this complex [ Co ( NH ₃ )₆ ] Cl ₃ ?
117872.sol: Primary valency of coordination compounds are ionisable. Thus, dissociation of the complex, [ Co ( NH ₃ )₆ ] Cl ₃ takes place as follows [ Co ( NH ₃ )₆ ] Cl ₃ [ Co ( NH ₃ )₆ ]²⁺+3 Cl ⁻ Therefore, total number of ions obtain will be 4 .

118808.subject: Chemistry
118808.text: Phenol is treated with aqueous sodium hydroxide followed by carbon dioxide gas, and the resulting mixture is acidified to give compound X. Compound X is then heated with acetic anhydride in the presence of a catalytic amount of concentrated H ₂ SO ₄ to yield compound Y. Identify the final product Y.
118808.sol: In the first step, phenol reacts with sodium hydroxide and carbon dioxide followed by acidification. This is Kolbe's reaction, which yields salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid) as compound X. In the second step, salicylic acid (X) undergoes acetylation when treated with acetic anhydride in the presence of concentrated H ₂ SO ₄ . The phenolic - OH group is acetylated to form acetylsalicylic acid, which is commonly known as aspirin (compound Y). If the first step had been the Reimer-Tiemann reaction, the intermedia

119406.subject: Chemistry
119406.text: Which one of the following reactions is called Rosenmund reaction?
options: Acids are converted to acid chlorides
Acid chlorides are reduced to aldehydes
119406.sol: In the Rosenmund's reaction acid chlorides are converted to corresponding aldehydes by catalytic reduction.

119533.subject: Chemistry
119533.text: Assertion : Nitration of benzoic acid gives ortho and para derivatives of nitrobenzoic acids. Reason : Carboxyl group is activating group.
options: If both Assertion & Reason are true and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion, then mark (1).
If both Assertion & Reason are true but the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion, then mark
If Assertion is true statement but Reason is false, then mark (3).
If both Assertion and Reason are false statements, then mark (4).
119533.sol: (- CO ₂ H ) is a deactivator because of its -M effect it gives meta product.

119706.subject: Chemistry
119706.text: What is the purpose of using metals like iron, zinc, and tin for the reduction of nitro compounds in an acidic medium?
119706.sol: These metals react with acids to release hydrogen gas, which reduces the nitro compounds.

120220.subject: Chemistry
120220.text: What does the classification system focus on regarding drug action?
options: The impact of drugs on biochemical processes
120220.sol: The classification is based on the action of a drug on a particular biochemical process.

120234.subject: Chemistry
120234.text: What is dysidazirine supposed to be toxic towards?
120234.sol: The antibiotic dysidazirine is supposed to be toxic towards certain strains of cancer cells.

120905.subject: Chemistry
120905.text: What are the common types of secondary structure of proteins?
options: The common types of secondary structure of proteins include primary and tertiary structures.
The common types of secondary structure of proteins are alpha helix and beta sheets.
The common types of secondary structure of proteins are globular and fibrous.
The common types of secondary structure of proteins are hydrophobic and hydrophilic regions.
120905.sol: Correct Option is : (B) The common types of secondary structure of proteins are alpha helix and beta sheets.

121293.subject: Botany
121293.text: What is the accumulation of diatom cell wall deposits over billions of years referred to as?
121293.sol: This group includes diatoms and golden algae (desmids). They are found in fresh water as well as in marine environments. They are microscopic and float passively in water currents (plankton). Most of them are photosynthetic. In diatoms the cell walls form two thin overlapping shells, which fit together as in a soap box. The walls are embedded with silica and thus the walls are indestructible. Thus, diatoms have left behind large amount of cell wall deposits in their habitat; this accumulation over billions of years

121817.subject: Botany
121817.text: In which plants can sporophylls form distinct compact structures called strobili or cones?
121817.sol: The Pteridophytes include horsetails and ferns. Pteridophytes are used for medicinal purposes and as soil-binders. They are also frequently grown as ornamentals. Evolutionarily, they are the first terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissues – xylem and phloem. The pteridophytes are found in cool, damp, shady places though some may flourish well in sandy-soil conditions. In pteridophytes, the main plant body is a sporophyte which is differentiated into true root, stem and leaves (Figure 3.3). These organs possess

122491.subject: Botany
122491.text: What are the reasons that you can think of for the arthropods to constitute the largest group of the animal kingdom?
options: Ability to live in diverse conditions and varied habitats
Well developed sense organs and nervous system
Hard skeletons reduce water loss from the body
122491.sol: Ability to live in diverse conditions and varied habitats, Well developed sense organs and nervous system, hard skeleton reduce water loss from the body

123038.subject: Botany
123038.text: Match List-I with List-II regarding aestivation in flowers. List-I (Type of Aestivation) List-II (Example) (A) Valvate (I) Bean (B) Twisted (II) Gulmohur (C) Imbricate (III) Cotton (D) Vexillary (IV) Calotropis Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
123038.sol: According to NCERT, in valvate aestivation, sepals or petals just touch one another at the margin without overlapping (e.g., Calotropis). In twisted aestivation, one margin of the appendage overlaps that of the next one (e.g., cotton). In imbricate aestivation, margins overlap but not in any particular direction (e.g., gulmohur). In vexillary aestivation, the largest petal overlaps the two lateral petals, which in turn overlap the two smallest anterior petals (e.g., bean). Therefore, the correct match is (A)-(IV),

123065.subject: Botany
123065.text: How many plants in the list given below have marginal placentation? Mustard, Gram, Tulip, Asparagus, Arhar, Sunnhemp, Chilli, Colchicine, Onion, Moong, Pea, Tobacco, Lupin

123070.subject: Botany
123070.text: The ovary is half inferior in flowers of
123070.sol: If gynoecium is situated in the center and other parts of the flowers are located on the rim of the thalamus almost at the same level, it is called perigynous. The ovary here is said to be half inferior, i.e., plum rose, peach, etc.

123143.subject: Botany
123143.text: Upon fertilization, what structure develops from carpel?
123143.sol: Ripened ovary or fertilized ovary is called fruit. The wall of the ovary forms fleshy or dry fruit wall known as pericarp. It means that the pericarp is developed from pistil or carpel.

123647.subject: Botany
123647.text: Are haploid cells capable of dividing by mitosis?
options: Yes, in some lower plants and social insects
No, mitosis is restricted to diploid cells only.
123647.sol: Mitosis or the equational division is usually restricted to the diploid cells only. However, in some lower plants and in some social insects haploid cells also divide by mitosis. It is very essential to understand the significance of this division in the life of an organism. Are you aware of some examples where you have studied about haploid and diploid insects? Mitosis usually results in the production of diploid daughter cells with identical genetic complement. The growth of multicellular organisms is due to mito

124202.subject: Botany
124202.text: Cell Size and Shape Example or Feature A. Mycoplasma 1. Largest isolated single cell B. Bacteria 2. Rod-like or spherical C. Nerve cells 3. Longest cells D. Ostrich egg 4. Smallest cell (0.3 μm)
124202.sol: Mycoplasma is the smallest cell, bacteria can be rod-like or spherical, nerve cells are the longest, and the ostrich egg is the largest isolated single cell.

124372.subject: Botany
124372.text: A spherical structure is observed within the nucleus. It is not membrane-bound and its content is continuous with the rest of the nucleoplasm. Which of the following is the primary cellular process that occurs within this structure?
124372.sol: According to NCERT, the nucleolus is a spherical structure present in the nucleoplasm. Since it is not membrane-bound, its content is continuous with the rest of the nucleoplasm. The primary function of the nucleolus is to serve as a site for active ribosomal RNA (rRNA) synthesis. Transcription of messenger RNA (mRNA) occurs generally in the nucleoplasm, protein synthesis occurs on ribosomes in the cytoplasm or rough endoplasmic reticulum, and lipid synthesis occurs in the smooth endoplasmic reticulum. Answer: Acti

124758.subject: Botany
124758.text: During the investigation of callus proliferation in tobacco stems, Miller et al. identified and crystallised a cytokinesis-promoting active substance termed kinetin. Based on its chemical composition, this plant growth regulator is classified as:
124758.sol: Miller et al. identified and crystallised kinetin, which is a cytokinesis-promoting active substance (a cytokinin). According to the chemical composition of plant growth regulators, cytokinins like kinetin ( N⁶ -furfurylamino purine) are modified purines, specifically adenine derivatives. Indole compounds refer to auxins (e.g., IAA), terpenes refer to gibberellins (e.g., GA₃ ), and derivatives of carotenoids refer to abscisic acid (ABA). Answer: An adenine derivative

125210.subject: Botany
125210.text: Which of the following is the connecting link between glycolysis and Krebs cycle?
125210.sol: Glycolysis is the first step of sepiration in which glucose is broken down to pyrurate. During glycolysis 1 molecule of glucose is converted to 2 molecules of pyruvic acid in the cytoplasm. These two molecules of pyruvic acid is then converted to acetyl CoA by decarboxylation. This acetyl CoA is the connecting link between glycolysis and Krebs' cycle and functions as substrate entrant for Krebs' cycle. Acetyl CoA thus formed participates in Krebs' cycle and combines with oxaloacetic acid to form citrate.

125322.subject: Botany
125322.text: What was described as a result of Engelmann's observations?
options: The absorption spectrum of chlorophyll c
The first action spectrum of photosynthesis
125322.sol: Now consider the interesting experiments done by T.W Engelmann (1843 – 1909). Using a prism he split light into its spectral components and then illuminated a green alga, Cladophora, placed in a suspension of aerobic bacteria. The bacteria were used to detect the sites of O2 evolution. He observed that the bacteria accumulated mainly in the region of blue and red light of the split spectrum. A first action spectrum of photosynthesis was thus described . It resembles roughly the absorption spectra of chlorophyll a a

125866.subject: Botany
125866.text: How do cleistogamous flowers ensure pollination?
options: By having anthers and stigma close to each other
125866.sol: Autogamy: In this type, pollination is achieved within the same flower. Transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of the same flower Autogamy in such flowers requires synchrony in pollen release and stigma receptivity and also, the anthers and the stigma should. lie close to each other so that self-pollination can occur. Some plants such as Viola (common pansy), Oxalis, and Commelina produce two types of flowers – chasmogamous flowers which are similar to flowers of other species with exposed anthers

125964.subject: Botany
125964.text: What is a seed often described as?
125964.sol: In angiosperms, the seed is the final product of sexual reproduction. It is often described as a fertilised ovule. Seeds are formed inside fruits. A seed typically consists of seed coat(s), cotyledon(s) and an embryo axis. The cotyledons (Figure 1.15a) of the embryo are simple structures, generally thick and swollen due to storage of food reserves (as in legumes). Mature seeds may be non-albuminous or ex-albuminous. Nonalbuminous seeds have no residual endosperm as it is completely consumed during embryo developmen

126021.subject: Botany
126021.text: Identify and name v,w,x,y and z respectively.
options: Endosperm, Cotyledon, Seed coat, Shoot apical meristem, Hypocotyl root axis
Seed coat, Endosperm, Cotyledon, Hypocotyl root axis, Shoot apical meristem
Shoot apical meristem, Endosperm, Cotyledon, Seed coat, Hypocotyl root axis
Seed coat, Endosperm, Cotyledon, Shoot apical meristem, Hypocotyl root axis

126049.subject: Botany
126049.text: Identify and name w,x,y and z respectively
options: Nucellus, Megaspore mother cell, Megaspore tetrad, Megaspore dyad
Nucellus, Megaspore mother cell, Megaspore dyad, Megaspore tetrad
Nucellus, Megaspore mother cell, Megaspore dyad, Megaspore tetrad
Nucellus, Megaspore mother cell, Megaspore tetrad, Megaspore dyad

126977.subject: Botany
126977.text: Due to increasing air-borne allergens and pollutants, many people in urban areas are suffering from respiratory disorder causing wheezing due to
options: benign growth on mucous lining of nasal cavity.
proliferation of fibrous tissues and damage of the alveolar walls.
reduction in the secretion of surfactants by pneumocytes.
126977.sol: Allergic bronchitis involves inflammation of the bronchi caused by an allergen, or something to which you are allergic. Airway irritants, such as pollen, dust, and mold, can trigger symptoms. It causes difficulty in breathing and followed with a severe cough, restlessness, cough and a wheezing sound while breathing.

127110.subject: Botany
127110.text: Which of the following statement is correct about DDT ?
options: It is a biomagnifying biodegradable pollutant
It is non biomagnifying biodegradable pollutant
It is biomagnifying non biodegradable pollutant
127110.sol: DDT has been recently banned because it is non-biodegradable and biomagnifying pollutant. Biomagnification means the increase in amount of DDT in the body of organism along with the increase in trophic level. Hence, the amount of DDT in 1st trophic level will be minimum and in top consumer will be maximum.

127306.subject: Botany
127306.text: Read the following statements and choose the following option: 1. The present rates of species losses can eliminate biodiversity in less than 2 centuries. 2. It has taken millions of years for nature to accumulate its diversity. 3. The loss of species diversity will take millions of years. 4. Biodiversity has developed rapidly in the last few centuries.
127306.sol: It has taken millions of years of evolution, to accumulate this rich diversity in nature, but we could lose all that wealth in less than two centuries if the present rates of species losses continue."

127389.subject: Botany
127389.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): The current Sixth Extinction is progressing at a rate estimated to be 10 to 50 times faster than in the pre-human times. Reason (R): Anthropogenic activities, primarily habitat loss and fragmentation, have drastically accelerated species extinction in recent times. In the light of the above stateme
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
127389.sol: The Assertion is false because according to NCERT, the current species extinction rates are estimated to be 100 to 1000 times faster than in the pre-human times, not 10 to 50 times. The Reason is true because human activities (anthropogenic factors), especially habitat loss and fragmentation, are the primary drivers of this accelerated extinction rate. Therefore, Assertion is false but Reason is true. Answer: Assertion is false but Reason is true.

127890.subject: Zoology
127890.text: What is the conventional use of the word anatomy?
options: Study of morphology of internal organs in animals
Study of external appearance in plants
127890.sol: The basic tissues as you have learnt in earlier classes, organise to form organs which in turn associate to form organ systems in the multicellular organisms. Such an organisation is essential for more efficient and better coordinated activities of millions of cells constituting an organism. Each organ in our body is made of one or more type of tissues. For example, our heart consists of all the four types of tissues, i.e., epithelial, connective, muscular and neural. We also notice, after some careful study that t

127916.subject: Zoology
127916.text: What feature distinguishes male frogs from female frogs?
options: Presence of vocal sacs and copulatory pad
127916.sol: . Have you ever touched the skin of frog? The skin is smooth and slippery due to the presence of mucus. The skin is always maintained in a moist condition. The colour of dorsal side of body is generally olive green with dark irregular spots. On the ventral side the skin is uniformly pale yellow. The frog never drinks water but absorb it through the skin. Body of a frog is divisible into head and trunk A neck and tail are absent. Above the mouth, a pair of nostrils is present. Eyes are bulged and covered by a nictit

128120.subject: Zoology
128120.text: Match List-I with List-II regarding connective tissues. List-I List-II (A) Areolar tissue (I) Attaches bone to bone (B) Adipose tissue (II) Attaches skeletal muscle to bone (C) Tendon (III) Serves as a support framework for epithelium (D) Ligament (IV) Specialised to store fats Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
128120.sol: Areolar tissue is a loose connective tissue that serves as a support framework for epithelium. Adipose tissue is another loose connective tissue specialised to store fats. Tendons are dense regular connective tissues that attach skeletal muscles to bones. Ligaments are dense regular connective tissues that attach one bone to another. Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)

128332.subject: Zoology
128332.text: What is the effect of the degeneration of the thymus gland in old individuals?
128332.sol: The thymus gland is a lobular structure located between lungs behind sternum on the ventral side of aorta. The thymus plays a major role in the development of the immune system. This gland secretes the peptide hormones called thymosins. Thymosins play a major role in the differentiation of T-lymphocytes, which provide cell-mediated immunity. In addition, thymosins also promote production of antibodies to provide humoral immunity . Thymus is degenerated in old individuals resulting in a decreased production of thymo

128410.subject: Zoology
128410.text: The pituitary gland is located in a bony cavity called ___A___ and is attached to __ B__ by a stalk Identify A and B to complete the given statement
128410.sol: The pituitary gland is located in a bony cavity called sella tursica and is attached to the hypothalamus by a stalk (Figure 22.2). It is divided anatomically into an adenohypophysis and a neurohypophysis. Adenohypophysis consists of two portions, pars distalis and pars intermedia.

129023.subject: Zoology
129023.text: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: A person of ‘O’ blood group has anti ‘A’ and anti ‘B’ antibodies in his blood plasma.
A person of ‘B’ blood group can’t donate blood to a person of ‘A’ blood group.
Blood group is designated based on the presence of antibodies in the blood plasma.
A person of the AB blood group is a universal recipient.
129023.sol: Blood group is designated based on the presence of antigen in the blood plasma.

129118.subject: Zoology
129118.text: Cattle fed with spoilt hay of sweet clover which contains dicumarol
options: are healthier due to a good diet
may suffer vitamin (K ) deficiency and prolonged bleeding
may suffer from beri-beri due to deficiency of vitamin (B₁ ).
129118.sol: Dicumarol is an anticoagulant found in spoilts sweet clover causes hemorrhage and other symptoms of bleeding disorder by disrupting vitamin K metabolism and preventing the activation of prothrombin and certain other clotting factors by the liver.

129260.subject: Zoology
129260.text: What does the cerebellum have in order to provide additional space for neurons?
129260.sol: The thalamus is a major coordinating center for sensory and motor signaling.The limbic system, along with the hypothalamus, is involved in the regulation of sexual behavior, expression of emotional reactions, and motivation.The amygdala, along with other structures of the limbic system, is involved in the expression of emotional reactions. The hippocampus, along with other structures of the limbic system, is involved in processing of memory and spatial navigation. The medulla of the brain contains centres which con

129701.subject: Zoology
129701.text: Which of the following physiological conditions most likely stimulates the release of Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH) from the neurohypophysis?
options: An increase in body fluid volume
An excessive loss of fluid from the body
129701.sol: Osmoreceptors in the body are activated by changes in blood volume, body fluid volume, and ionic concentration. An excessive loss of fluid from the body can activate these receptors, which stimulate the hypothalamus to release Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH) or vasopressin from the neurohypophysis. ADH facilitates water reabsorption from latter parts of the tubule, thereby preventing diuresis. An increase in body fluid volume or high intake of water switches off the osmoreceptors and suppresses ADH release to complete t

129742.subject: Zoology
129742.text: Refer the given figure of nephron. Identify A, B, C and D and select the correct option regarding them
options: A-Glomerulus - a tuft of capillaries formed by afferent arteriole
B-PCT-reabsorption of HCO ₃⁻ and selective secretion of H ⁺ and K ⁺ occurs here.
C-DCT-almost all glucose, amino acids, water, Na ⁺, K ⁺ and uric acid are absorbed here.
D-collecting duct-extends from the cortex of the kidney to the inner parts of medulla. Large amount of water i

129915.subject: Zoology
129915.text: What is the first step in respiration?
options: Exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide between deoxygenated blood and alveoli
Transport of gases throughout the body by blood
Exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide between oxygenated blood and tissues
129915.sol: The first step in respiration is breathing by which atmospheric air is taken in (inspiration) and the alveolar air is released out (expiration). Respiration involves the following steps: (i) Breathing or pulmonary ventilation by which atmospheric air is drawn in and CO2 rich alveolar air is released out. (ii) Diffusion of gases (O2 and CO2) across alveolar membrane. (iii) Transport of gases by the blood. (iv) Diffusion of O2 and CO2 between blood and tissues. (v) Utilisation of O2 by the cells for catabolic reactio

130124.subject: Zoology
130124.text: When a man inhales air containing normal concentration of ( O ₂ ) as well as ( CO ) he suffers from suffocation because
options: ( CO ) reacts with ( O ₂ ) reducing its percentage in air
haemoglobin combines with ( CO ) instead of ( O ₂ ) and forms carboxyhaemoglobin
( CO ) affects diaphragm and intercostal muscles
( CO ) affects the nerves of the lungs.
130124.sol: Affinity of carbon monoxide for haemoglobin is 200 times more than oxygen. At 0.5 partial pressure, CO combines with 50 % of haemoglobin. It produces a relatively stable compound called carboxy-haemoglobin. This causes low supply of oxygen to the body which is characterised by headache, dizziness, nausea, etc.

130643.subject: Zoology
130643.text: Female condoms are inserted into which part of the body to prevent pregnancy and sexually transmitted infections (STIs)?
130643.sol: In barrier methods, ovum and sperms are prevented from physically meeting with the help of barriers. Such methods are available for both males and females. Condoms (Figure 3.1 a, b) are barriers made of thin rubber/ latex sheath that are used to cover the penis in the male or vagina and cervix in the female, just before coitus so that the ejaculated semen would not enter into the female reproductive tract. This can prevent conception.

131211.subject: Zoology
131211.text: Match List I with List II regarding the cells of spermatogenesis in humans, their chromosome number, and the immediate next physiological process they undergo. List I List II A. Spermatogonia I. 23 chromosomes, undergoes meiosis II B. Primary spermatocyte II. 46 chromosomes, undergoes meiosis I C. Secondary spermatocyte III. 23 chromosomes, undergoes spermiogenesis D. Spermatid IV. 46 chromosomes, undergoes mitosis C
131211.sol: Spermatogonia are diploid cells on the inside wall of seminiferous tubules containing 46 chromosomes, and they multiply by mitotic division. Some spermatogonia differentiate into primary spermatocytes, which are also diploid (46 chromosomes) and undergo the first meiotic division (meiosis I). If both assertion and reason are false.

Its granulosa cells continue to proliferate, develop yellow carotene pigment or lutein and get converted into lutein cells. This converts the ruptured follicle into yellow body called corpus luteum. 131533.text: Who argued that the code should consist of a combination of three nucleotides to code for 20 amino acids?
131533.sol: If determining the biochemical nature of genetic material and the structure of DNA was very exciting, the proposition and deciphering of genetic code were most challenging. In a very true sense, it required involvement of scientists from several disciplines – physicists, organic chemists, biochemists and geneticists. It was George Gamow, a physicist, who argued that since there are only 4 bases and if they have to code for 20 amino acids, the code should constitute a combination of bases. 131944.subject: Zoology
131944.text: Which organism is used to transfer T-DNA?
131944.sol: Ti plasmid (tumour inducing) from the soil bacterium Agrobacterium tumefaciens is effectively used as vector for gene transfer to plant cells. The part of Ti plasmid transferred into plant cell DNA, is called the T-DNA. This T-DNA with desired DNA spliced into it, is inserted into the chromosome of the host plant where it produces copies of itself, by migrating from one chromosomal position to another at random.

131955.sol: Non sense codon or terminator codon are the codons that do not code for any amino acid. It is a set of three nucleotides for which there is no corresponding tRNA molecule to insert an amino acid into the polypeptide chain. Protein synthesis is hence terminated and the completed polypeptide released from the ribosome. Three stop codons are UAA (ochre), UAG (amber) and UGA (opal). Increasing the number of water-borne diseases
Discharging only treated sewage in the rivers

133811.subject: Zoology
133811.text: What is the function of Baculoviruses in biological control?
options: To attack insects and other arthropods
To aid in integrated pest management
To have negative impacts on the environment
133811.sol: Baculoviruses are pathogens that attack insects and other arthropods. The majority of baculoviruses used as biological control agents are in the genus Nucleopolyhedrovirus. These viruses are excellent candidates for species-specific, narrow spectrum insecticidal applications. They have been shown to have no negative impacts on plants, mammals, birds, fish or even on non-target insects. This is especially desirable when beneficial insects are being conserved to aid in an overall integrated pest management (IPM) prog

133958.subject: Zoology
133958.text: The puffed-up appearance of dough used for making bread is due to the production of CO ₂ gas. Which of the following correctly identifies the biological agent responsible for this and the metabolic process involved?
133958.sol: The dough used for making bread is fermented using baker's yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae). The puffed-up appearance of dough is due to the production of CO ₂ gas. This gas is produced during fermentation, which is a type of anaerobic respiration. Lactobacillus is primarily used in curd formation, while Propionibacterium sharmanii is responsible for the large holes in Swiss cheese. Answer: Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Anaerobic respiration

Presence of two or more recognition sites
134945.sol: The term cloning vectors refer to the DNA molecules that act as transporting vehicle which carries foreign DNA into a host cell for cloning and expression. They are more adversely affected by competition compared to carnivores
They benefit from competition more than carnivores

6a2a77befad2360f42564bcf.subject: Biology
6a2a77befad2360f42564bcf.text: Which of the following statements correctly describes the condition of ovules in gymnosperms?
options: They are enclosed by an ovary wall before fertilization but become exposed later.
They are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed both before and after fertilization.
They are completely enclosed within a fruit post-fertilization.
They remain exposed before fertilization but are covered by a fleshy pericarp after fertilization.
6a2a77befad2360f42564bcf.sol: Gymnosperms (gymnos = naked, sperma = seeds) are plants in which the ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed, both before and after fertilization. The seeds that develop post-fertilization are not covered, i.e., they are naked. Therefore, the statement that they are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed both before and after fertilization is correct. Answer: They are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed both before and after fertilization.
